key_insight: Bayesian inference on photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion simulations can localize where perovskite solar cells degrade, separating bulk from interface-driven failure.
engineering_relevance: The method helps engineers diagnose the dominant degradation pathway in real devices, enabling more targeted material and interface design for longer-lived perovskite modules.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated devices
Drift-diffusion simulation linked to Bayesian parameter inference
Temporal tracking of inferred recombination maps during aging
evidence_signal: Devices were aged under 70 °C full-spectrum sunlight, and the inferred parameter maps showed pronounced spatially non-uniform degradation that was strongest at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The approach depends on model fidelity and imaging quality, so inferred degradation locations may be sensitive to assumptions in the drift-diffusion framework and inverse problem setup.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
